correctness.rationale: On the specified ten intersecting two-subsets, the replay reconstructs both synchronous threshold-one successor maps and processes all 59,049 labelled colorings. Indegree-zero deletion leaves exactly the directed cycles, and reverse deletion assigns the exact entry time and least period from each successor. The two period arrays match pointwise (3,399 with period 1; 55,650 with period 3); the entire joint census matches, with sharp entry cutoffs 2 and 4. There are 30,240 common primitive-three recurrent states, exactly those with a successor-color neighbor at every vertex. On them both rules increment every site, which preserves that condition and gives least period three. This is not equality on the entire recurrent sets: the fixed point counts are 3 and 1. The five size-four cliques are exactly the stars of K5; a pairwise-intersecting family with no common point is contained in a triangle. Thus every automorphism permutes the five stars, recovering all and only S5. Replaying the spatial action modulo the three phases partitions 10,080 cycles into 118 orbits with size/count pairs (15,2), (20,3), (30,7), (60,49), (120,57). This certifies only the specified finite graph and rules. The uploaded artifacts were inspected, not executed.

value.rationale: Comparing Petersen with its canonical complement tests whether the documented period mismatch persists under changing disjointness to intersection. The answer is not just agreement of fixed-point basin sizes: the same nontrivial cycles occur but with markedly different entry clocks, and the exact phase-quotiented orbit histogram gives a benchmark for geometric classification of these waves. This motivation is specific to the object and observables, without implying an infinite-family theorem.
